title: Advanced Usage
text: vignette covers advanced usage scenarios scPharm, including: Custom threshold calibration Multi-drug analysis strategies Combination therapy optimization Integration external tools Performance tuning
code: library(ggplot2) library(dplyr)

title: Advanced Usage
text: accurate cell classification, calibrating thresholds using normal tissue samples recommended:
code: library(scPharm)  # Load normal tissue reference normal_seurat <- readRDS("normal_tissue.rds")  # Generate null distribution null_dist <- scPharmGenNullDist(   normal_seurat,   cancer = "LUAD",   drug = "Erlotinib",   nmcs = 50,   nfeatures = 200 )  # Extract calibrated thresholds threshold_s <- null_dist$threshold.s threshold_r <- null_dist$threshold.r  cat("Sensitive threshold:", threshold_s, "\n") cat("Resistant threshold:", threshold_r, "\n")

title: Advanced Usage
code: # Load tumor sample tumor_seurat <- readRDS("tumor_sample.rds")  # Run analysis with calibrated thresholds result <- scPharmIdentify(   tumor_seurat,   type = "tissue",   cancer = "LUAD",   drug = "Erlotinib",   threshold.s = threshold_s,   threshold.r = threshold_r )

title: Advanced Usage
code: # Analyze all available drugs result_all <- scPharmIdentify(   seurat_obj,   type = "cellline",   cancer = "BRCA",   drug = "all",   cores = 8  # Parallel processing )  # Get drug ranking dr_scores <- scPharmDr(result_all) print(head(dr_scores, 20))

title: Advanced Usage
code: # Load drug metadata data(drug_info, package = "scPharm")  # Filter by drug class chemo_drugs <- drug_info %>%   filter(DRUG_TYPE == "chemotherapy") %>%   pull(DRUG_NAME)  targeted_drugs <- drug_info %>%   filter(DRUG_TYPE == "targeted") %>%   pull(DRUG_NAME)  # Analyze specific drug classes result_chemo <- scPharmIdentify(   seurat_obj,   cancer = "BRCA",   drug = chemo_drugs )  result_targeted <- scPharmIdentify(   seurat_obj,   cancer = "BRCA",   drug = targeted_drugs )

title: Advanced Usage
code: # Analyze across multiple cancer contexts cancers <- c("BRCA", "LUAD", "COREAD")  results <- lapply(cancers, function(cancer) {   result <- scPharmIdentify(     seurat_obj,     type = "cellline",     cancer = cancer,     drug = "Paclitaxel"   )      # Extract NES values   nes_col <- grep("scPharm_nes_", colnames(result@meta.data), value = TRUE)   data.frame(     cancer = cancer,     mean_nes = mean(result@meta.data[[nes_col]], na.rm = TRUE),     sd_nes = sd(result@meta.data[[nes_col]], na.rm = TRUE)   ) })  # Combine results multi_cancer_df <- do.call(rbind, results) print(multi_cancer_df)

title: Advanced Usage
code: # Get drug ranking first dr_scores <- scPharmDr(result)  # Identify combinations for top drugs combos <- scPharmCombo(result, dr_scores, topN = 10)  # Examine results for (drug_name in names(combos)) {   cat("\n=== Drug:", drug_name, "===\n")   print(head(combos[[drug_name]]$combination_scores)) }

title: Advanced Usage
text: combination score considers: Complementarity: drugs target different resistant populations? Coverage: percentage resistant cells become sensitive? Synergy potential: Based known drug interactions Drug combination evaluation

title: Advanced Usage
code: # Use existing Seurat clustering seurat_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(seurat_obj) seurat_obj <- ScaleData(seurat_obj) seurat_obj <- RunPCA(seurat_obj) seurat_obj <- FindNeighbors(seurat_obj) seurat_obj <- FindClusters(seurat_obj) seurat_obj <- RunUMAP(seurat_obj, dims = 1:30)  # Run scPharm (MCA is computed independently) result <- scPharmIdentify(seurat_obj, ...)  # Visualize with Seurat functions DimPlot(result, group.by = "scPharm_label_Docetaxel") FeaturePlot(result, features = "scPharm_nes_Docetaxel")

title: Advanced Usage
code: # Aggregate NES by cluster cluster_summary <- result@meta.data %>%   group_by(seurat_clusters) %>%   summarise(     n_cells = n(),     mean_nes = mean(scPharm_nes_Docetaxel, na.rm = TRUE),     pct_sensitive = mean(scPharm_label_Docetaxel == "sensitive") * 100,     pct_resistant = mean(scPharm_label_Docetaxel == "resistant") * 100   )  print(cluster_summary)

title: Advanced Usage
text: large datasets, consider:
code: # Process in chunks cell_chunks <- split(colnames(seurat_obj),                       ceiling(seq_along(colnames(seurat_obj)) / 5000))  results <- lapply(cell_chunks, function(cells) {   subset_obj <- subset(seurat_obj, cells = cells)   scPharmIdentify(subset_obj, ...) })  # Merge results final_result <- merge(results[[1]], results[-1])

title: Advanced Usage
code: # Detect available cores n_cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1  # Run with multiple cores result <- scPharmIdentify(   seurat_obj,   drug = "all",   cores = n_cores )

title: Advanced Usage
code: # Load custom drug sensitivity signatures custom_signatures <- list(   DrugA_sensitive = c("GENE1", "GENE2", "GENE3", ...),   DrugA_resistant = c("GENE4", "GENE5", "GENE6", ...) )  # Note: This requires modifying internal functions # Contact maintainer for custom signature integration

title: Advanced Usage
code: # Check gene coverage data(bulkdata, package = "scPharm") gene_overlap <- intersect(rownames(seurat_obj), rownames(bulkdata)) cat("Gene overlap:", length(gene_overlap), "/", nrow(bulkdata), "\n")  # Minimum recommended: 5000 genes if (length(gene_overlap) < 5000) {   warning("Low gene overlap may affect accuracy") }  # Check cell numbers if (ncol(seurat_obj) < 100) {   warning("Small cell numbers may lead to unstable estimates") }

title: Advanced Usage
code: # Check NES distribution nes_values <- result@meta.data$scPharm_nes_Docetaxel  # Should be roughly normal/bimodal hist(nes_values, breaks = 50, main = "NES Distribution")  # Check classification balance table(result@meta.data$scPharm_label_Docetaxel)

title: Advanced Usage
code: # Verbose output options(scPharm.verbose = TRUE)  # Step-by-step execution result <- scPharmIdentify(   seurat_obj,   type = "cellline",   cancer = "BRCA",   drug = "Docetaxel" )

title: Advanced Usage
code: # Extract all scPharm columns scpharm_cols <- grep("^scPharm_|^cell\\.label$",                       colnames(result@meta.data), value = TRUE)  export_df <- result@meta.data[, scpharm_cols] export_df$cell_id <- rownames(export_df)  write.csv(export_df, "scpharm_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: scPharm employs multi-step computational pipeline identify pharmacological subpopulations single-cell resolution. vignette describes underlying algorithms statistical methods.

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: scPharm analytical workflow

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: tissue samples containing mixed tumor normal cells, scPharm employs integrated CopyKAT-based algorithm distinguish malignant cells.

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: CNV detection follows steps: Gene Annotation: Map genes chromosomal positions using hg20 annotations Expression Binning: Aggregate expression genomic bins (220 bins per chromosome) Baseline Normalization: Use normal cells synthetic baseline reference Smoothing: Apply Kalman filtering reduce noise Clustering: Hierarchical clustering identify aneuploid populations

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: gene gg genomic position pp, relative copy number estimated : CNVg=log⁡2(EgtumorEgbaseline+1)\text{CNV}_{g} = \log_2\left(\frac{E_g^{tumor}}{E_g^{baseline}} + 1\right) EgE_g represents normalized expression level. CNV profile across chromosomes

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: MCA used dimensionality reduction, preserving correspondence genes cells.

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: Unlike PCA assumes continuous data, MCA designed categorical/count data provides: Joint embedding cells genes Natural handling sparse scRNA-seq data Interpretable gene-cell associations

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: Given normalized expression matrix 𝐗\mathbf{X} nn cells pp genes: Construct indicator matrix 𝐙\mathbf{Z} discretizing expression levels Compute correspondence matrix: 𝐒=𝐃r−1/2(𝐙−𝐫𝐜T)𝐃c−1/2\mathbf{S} = \mathbf{D}_r^{-1/2}(\mathbf{Z} - \mathbf{rc}^T)\mathbf{D}_c^{-1/2} Perform SVD: 𝐒=𝐔𝚺𝐕T\mathbf{S} = \mathbf{U\Sigma V}^T Cell coordinates: 𝐅=𝐃r−1/2𝐔𝚺\mathbf{F} = \mathbf{D}_r^{-1/2}\mathbf{U\Sigma} Gene coordinates: 𝐆=𝐃c−1/2𝐕𝚺\mathbf{G} = \mathbf{D}_c^{-1/2}\mathbf{V\Sigma} MCA embedding showing cell-gene correspondence

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: scPharm implements MCA using RcppArmadillo computational efficiency:
code: // Simplified MCA computation (actual implementation in src/mca.cpp) arma::mat SparseMCAStep1(arma::sp_mat& X) {     // Column sums and total     arma::vec col_sum = arma::vec(arma::sum(X, 0).t());     double total = arma::accu(X);          // Compute standardized residuals     arma::mat Z = compute_residuals(X, col_sum, total);          return Z; }

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: cell, extract gene signature based position MCA space.

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: association cell ii gene jj computed : dij=∑k=1K(Fik−Gjk)2d_{ij} = \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^{K} (F_{ik} - G_{jk})^2} KK number MCA components.

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: cell, top nn genes (distance) form identity signature: Signaturei={g1,g2,...,gn} di,g1<di,g2<...<di,gn\text{Signature}_i = \{g_1, g_2, ..., g_n\} \text{ } d_{,g_1} < d_{,g_2} < ... < d_{,g_n}

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: GSEA quantifies enrichment drug sensitivity genes within cell’s signature.

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: Rank genes association cell Calculate running enrichment score (ES): ES=maxj(∑gi∈S,≤jN−|S||S|−∑gi∉S,≤j|S|N−|S|)ES = \max_{j}\left(\sum_{g_i \S, \leq j} \sqrt{\frac{N-|S|}{|S|}} - \sum_{g_i \notin S, \leq j} \sqrt{\frac{|S|}{N-|S|}}\right) Normalize obtain NES (Normalized Enrichment Score) GSEA running enrichment score

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: Drug sensitivity gene sets derived GDSC2 database: drug, genes ranked correlation IC50 Top correlated genes → Sensitivity signature Bottom correlated genes → Resistance signature

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: Cell NES values modeled mixture Gaussian distributions: P(NES)=πS⋅𝒩(μS,σS2)+πR⋅𝒩(μR,σR2)+πO⋅𝒩(μO,σO2)P(\text{NES}) = \pi_S \cdot \mathcal{N}(\mu_S, \sigma_S^2) + \pi_R \cdot \mathcal{N}(\mu_R, \sigma_R^2) + \pi_O \cdot \mathcal{N}(\mu_O, \sigma_O^2) Gaussian Mixture Model cell classification

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: Cells classified based NES thresholds:

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: Dr=1−(α⋅nSntumor+β⋅NES¯S)Dr = 1 - \left(\alpha \cdot \frac{n_S}{n_{tumor}} + \beta \cdot \overline{\text{NES}}_S\right) : - nSn_S = number sensitive cells - ntumorn_{tumor} = total tumor cells - NES¯S\overline{\text{NES}}_S = mean NES sensitive cells - α,β\alpha, \beta = weighting parameters Interpretation: Lower Dr indicates better drug candidate.

title: Algorithm and Methodology
text: Dse=nS,adjnadj⋅NES¯S,adjDse = \frac{n_{S,adj}}{n_{adj}} \cdot \overline{\text{NES}}_{S,adj} subscript adjadj denotes adjacent (non-tumor) cells. Interpretation: Higher Dse indicates potential side effects.

title: Quick Start Guide
text: scPharm computational framework identifying pharmacological subpopulations single cells cancer research. integrating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data pharmacogenomics profiles GDSC2 database, scPharm enables: Classification cells drug-sensitive drug-resistant subpopulations Prioritization therapeutic agents based tumor cell sensitivity Prediction drug side effects non-malignant cells Identification synergistic drug combinations vignette provides quick introduction get started scPharm.

title: Quick Start Guide
code: # From R-universe (recommended) install.packages("scPharm", repos = "https://zaoqu-liu.r-universe.dev")  # From GitHub remotes::install_github("Zaoqu-Liu/scPharm")

title: Quick Start Guide
code: library(scPharm) library(Seurat) library(ggplot2)

title: Quick Start Guide
text: demonstration, ’ll create simulated Seurat object genes matching GDSC2 database.
code: # Load reference gene annotations data(bulkdata, package = "scPharm") data(copykat_full.anno.hg20, package = "scPharm")  # Get real gene names real_genes <- intersect(rownames(bulkdata), copykat_full.anno.hg20$hgnc_symbol)  # Create simulated data set.seed(42) genes <- sample(real_genes, 3000) n_cells <- 200  # Simulate count matrix counts <- matrix(rpois(length(genes) * n_cells, lambda = 10),                   nrow = length(genes), ncol = n_cells) rownames(counts) <- genes colnames(counts) <- paste0("Cell_", seq_len(n_cells))  # Add variation high_var_genes <- sample(length(genes), 300) counts[high_var_genes, ] <- counts[high_var_genes, ] +    rpois(300 * n_cells, lambda = 25)  # Create Seurat object seurat_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts,                                    min.cells = 3,                                    min.features = 200) seurat_obj <- NormalizeData(seurat_obj, verbose = FALSE)  print(seurat_obj) #> An object of class Seurat  #> 3000 features across 200 samples within 1 assay  #> Active assay: RNA (3000 features, 0 variable features)

title: Quick Start Guide
text: core function scPharmIdentify() classifies cells based drug response profiles. tissue samples tumor/normal cell mixtures:
code: # For cell line data (no CNV detection needed) result <- scPharmIdentify(   seurat_obj,   type = "cellline",      # or "tissue" for patient samples    cancer = "BRCA",        # TCGA cancer type   drug = "Docetaxel",     # Drug name or "all"   nmcs = 30,              # Number of MCA components   nfeatures = 150,        # Features for cell signatures   cores = 4               # Parallel cores ) # Automatic tumor detection via CNV analysis result <- scPharmIdentify(   seurat_obj,   type = "tissue",   cancer = "LUAD" )  # Or provide known tumor cell barcodes tumor_cells <- c("Cell_1", "Cell_2", "Cell_3", ...) result <- scPharmIdentify(   seurat_obj,   type = "tissue",   cancer = "LUAD",   tumor.cells = tumor_cells )

title: Quick Start Guide
text: Rank drugs effectiveness tumor cells:
code: # Compute drug prioritization scores dr_scores <- scPharmDr(result)  # View top drugs head(dr_scores)

title: Quick Start Guide
text: tissue samples, estimate potential toxicity non-malignant cells:
code: # Compute drug side effect scores dse_scores <- scPharmDse(result)  # View results head(dse_scores)

title: Quick Start Guide
text: Find synergistic drug pairs targeting complementary resistant populations:
code: # Identify combinations for top 5 drugs combos <- scPharmCombo(result, dr_scores, topN = 5)  # View combination results names(combos)

title: Visualization Guide
text: vignette demonstrates various visualization strategies scPharm analysis results. Effective visualization crucial interpreting pharmacological heterogeneity single-cell resolution.
code: library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(patchwork)  # Define color palette scpharm_colors <- list(   sensitive = "#27ae60",   resistant = "#e74c3c",   other = "#95a5a6",   tumor = "#3498db",   adjacent = "#f39c12" )

title: Visualization Guide
text: demonstration, create simulated scPharm results.
code: set.seed(42) n_cells <- 500  # Simulate UMAP coordinates umap_data <- data.frame(   UMAP1 = c(rnorm(200, -3, 1), rnorm(150, 3, 1), rnorm(150, 0, 1.5)),   UMAP2 = c(rnorm(200, 2, 1), rnorm(150, 2, 1), rnorm(150, -2, 1.2)),   cell_label = c(rep("tumor", 350), rep("adjacent", 150)),   drug_label = c(     rep("sensitive", 150), rep("resistant", 100), rep("other", 100),     sample(c("sensitive", "resistant", "other"), 150,             replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.1, 0.1, 0.8))   ),   NES = c(     rnorm(150, 1.5, 0.4),   # Sensitive tumor     rnorm(100, -1.2, 0.4),  # Resistant tumor     rnorm(100, 0, 0.5),     # Other tumor     rnorm(150, 0, 0.6)      # Adjacent   ),   cell_id = paste0("Cell_", 1:n_cells) )  # Drug ranking data drug_ranking <- data.frame(   DRUG_NAME = c("Docetaxel", "Paclitaxel", "Erlotinib", "Gefitinib",                  "Tamoxifen", "Cisplatin", "Doxorubicin", "Imatinib"),   Dr = c(0.15, 0.22, 0.35, 0.42, 0.55, 0.61, 0.72, 0.85),   Dse = c(0.25, 0.18, 0.45, 0.32, 0.12, 0.55, 0.48, 0.22),   sensitive_pct = c(0.42, 0.38, 0.32, 0.28, 0.22, 0.20, 0.15, 0.08) )

title: Visualization Guide
text: UMAP visualization colored cell type
code: ggplot(umap_data, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = cell_label)) +   geom_point(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +   scale_color_manual(     values = c("tumor" = scpharm_colors$tumor,                 "adjacent" = scpharm_colors$adjacent),     name = "Cell Type"   ) +   labs(     title = "Cell Type Distribution",     subtitle = "Tumor vs Adjacent cells identified by CNV analysis",     x = "UMAP 1", y = "UMAP 2"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),     legend.position = "right"   ) +   guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4)))

text: NES distribution histogram
code: ggplot(umap_data, aes(x = NES, fill = cell_label)) +   geom_histogram(bins = 40, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +   geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c("tumor" = scpharm_colors$tumor,                 "adjacent" = scpharm_colors$adjacent),     name = "Cell Type"   ) +   annotate("text", x = -1.5, y = 40, label = "Resistant\nThreshold",             size = 3, color = "gray40") +   annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = 40, label = "Sensitive\nThreshold",             size = 3, color = "gray40") +   labs(     title = "NES Distribution by Cell Type",     x = "Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)",     y = "Count"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

text: NES density drug response classification
code: tumor_data <- umap_data[umap_data$cell_label == "tumor", ]  ggplot(tumor_data, aes(x = NES, fill = drug_label, color = drug_label)) +   geom_density(alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c("sensitive" = scpharm_colors$sensitive,                "resistant" = scpharm_colors$resistant,                "other" = scpharm_colors$other),     name = "Classification"   ) +   scale_color_manual(     values = c("sensitive" = scpharm_colors$sensitive,                "resistant" = scpharm_colors$resistant,                "other" = scpharm_colors$other),     name = "Classification"   ) +   labs(     title = "NES Density Distribution (Tumor Cells)",     x = "Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)",     y = "Density"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

title: Visualization Guide
text: NES violin plot cell type drug response
code: ggplot(umap_data, aes(x = interaction(cell_label, drug_label),                         y = NES, fill = drug_label)) +   geom_violin(alpha = 0.7, scale = "width") +   geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, outlier.size = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c("sensitive" = scpharm_colors$sensitive,                "resistant" = scpharm_colors$resistant,                "other" = scpharm_colors$other),     name = "Drug Response"   ) +   labs(     title = "NES Distribution by Cell Type and Drug Response",     x = "Cell Type × Drug Response",     y = "NES"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),     axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)   )

title: Visualization Guide
text: Drug prioritization ranking
code: drug_ranking <- drug_ranking[order(drug_ranking$Dr), ] drug_ranking$DRUG_NAME <- factor(drug_ranking$DRUG_NAME,                                    levels = drug_ranking$DRUG_NAME)  ggplot(drug_ranking, aes(x = DRUG_NAME, y = Dr, fill = Dr)) +   geom_col(width = 0.7) +   geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Dr)),              vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5) +   scale_fill_gradient(low = scpharm_colors$sensitive,                        high = scpharm_colors$resistant,                       name = "Dr Score") +   labs(     title = "Drug Prioritization Ranking",     subtitle = "Lower Dr score indicates better drug candidate",     x = "Drug",     y = "Drug Prioritization Score (Dr)"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),     axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)   ) +   coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1))

title: Visualization Guide
text: Drug efficacy vs side effects
code: ggplot(drug_ranking, aes(x = Dr, y = Dse, label = DRUG_NAME)) +   geom_point(aes(size = sensitive_pct, color = Dr), alpha = 0.8) +   geom_text(vjust = -1.2, size = 3.5) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0.3, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +   geom_vline(xintercept = 0.4, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +   scale_color_gradient(low = scpharm_colors$sensitive,                         high = scpharm_colors$resistant,                        name = "Dr Score") +   scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 12), name = "Sensitive %") +   annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 0.4, ymin = 0, ymax = 0.3,            fill = scpharm_colors$sensitive, alpha = 0.1) +   annotate("text", x = 0.2, y = 0.15, label = "Optimal\nRegion",            size = 4, fontface = "bold", color = scpharm_colors$sensitive) +   labs(     title = "Drug Efficacy vs Side Effects",     subtitle = "Optimal drugs: low Dr (effective) and low Dse (safe)",     x = "Drug Prioritization Score (Dr)",     y = "Drug Side Effect Score (Dse)"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),     legend.position = "right"   ) +   coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 0.7))

title: Visualization Guide
text: Cell proportion drug response
code: # Calculate proportions prop_data <- umap_data %>%   filter(cell_label == "tumor") %>%   count(drug_label) %>%   mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100)  ggplot(prop_data, aes(x = "", y = pct, fill = drug_label)) +   geom_col(width = 0.6) +   geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct)),             position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),              color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 5) +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c("sensitive" = scpharm_colors$sensitive,                "resistant" = scpharm_colors$resistant,                "other" = scpharm_colors$other),     name = "Drug Response"   ) +   labs(     title = "Tumor Cell Composition",     subtitle = "Proportion of cells by drug response classification",     y = "Percentage (%)"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),     axis.title.x = element_blank(),     axis.text.x = element_blank()   ) +   coord_flip()

title: Visualization Guide
text: Heatmap drug effects across cell clusters
code: # Simulate multi-drug data set.seed(123) drugs <- c("Docetaxel", "Paclitaxel", "Erlotinib", "Tamoxifen", "Cisplatin") clusters <- paste0("Cluster_", 1:8)  heatmap_data <- expand.grid(Drug = drugs, Cluster = clusters) %>%   mutate(     Mean_NES = rnorm(n(), 0, 0.8),     Mean_NES = case_when(       Drug == "Docetaxel" & Cluster %in% c("Cluster_1", "Cluster_2") ~ Mean_NES + 1.5,       Drug == "Paclitaxel" & Cluster %in% c("Cluster_1", "Cluster_3") ~ Mean_NES + 1.2,       Drug == "Erlotinib" & Cluster %in% c("Cluster_4", "Cluster_5") ~ Mean_NES + 1.0,       Drug == "Cisplatin" & Cluster %in% c("Cluster_6", "Cluster_7") ~ Mean_NES - 1.0,       TRUE ~ Mean_NES     )   )  ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = Cluster, y = Drug, fill = Mean_NES)) +   geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +   geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", Mean_NES)),              size = 3, color = "black") +   scale_fill_gradient2(     low = scpharm_colors$resistant,     mid = "white",     high = scpharm_colors$sensitive,     midpoint = 0,     name = "Mean NES"   ) +   labs(     title = "Drug Sensitivity Across Cell Clusters",     subtitle = "Mean NES values per drug-cluster combination",     x = "Cell Cluster",     y = "Drug"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),     axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),     panel.grid = element_blank()   )

NES Distribution", x = "NES", y = "Count") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),         legend.position = "bottom")  # Panel C: Drug ranking p3 <- ggplot(drug_ranking, aes(x = DRUG_NAME, y = Dr, fill = Dr)) +   geom_col(width = 0.7) +   scale_fill_gradient(low = scpharm_colors$sensitive,                        high = scpharm_colors$resistant,                       guide = "none") +   labs(title = "C. Drug Ranking", x = "Drug", y = "Dr Score") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),         axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))  # Panel D: Cell proportions p4 <- ggplot(prop_data, aes(x = "", y = pct, fill = drug_label)) +   geom_col(width = 1) +   coord_polar(theta = "y") +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c("sensitive" = scpharm_colors$sensitive,                "resistant" = scpharm_colors$resistant,                "other" = scpharm_colors$other),     name = "Response"   ) +   labs(title = "D. Cell Proportions") +   theme_void() +   theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0.5),         legend.position = "bottom")  # Combine panels (p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4) +   plot_annotation(     title = "scPharm Analysis Summary",     subtitle = "Comprehensive visualization of pharmacological heterogeneity",     theme = theme(       plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),       plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "gray40")     )   )

title: scPharm - Single-Cell Pharmacogenomics
text: Intratumoral heterogeneity poses significant challenge effective cancer treatment, diverse cellular subpopulations within tumor may exhibit distinct drug response profiles. scPharm computational framework integrates single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data pharmacogenomics profiles Genomics Drug Sensitivity Cancer (GDSC2) database dissect therapeutic heterogeneity single-cell resolution. framework employs Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA) dimensionality reduction Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) quantify drug sensitivity signatures, enabling classification individual cells pharmacologically distinct subpopulations.

title: Compute Drug Prioritization Score (Dr) — scPharmDr
text: Dr score calculated : $$Dr = S \times (1 - R)$$ S proportion sensitive cells R proportion resistant cells among tumor cells. Higher scores indicate better drug candidates patient.

title: Identify Pharmacological Cell Subpopulations — scPharmIdentify
code: scPharmIdentify(   object,   type,   cancer,   drug = NULL,   nmcs = 50,   nfeatures = 200,   cores = 1,   features = NULL,   slot = "data",   layer = NULL,   assay = "RNA",   threshold.s = -1.751302,   threshold.r = 1.518551,   tumor.cells = NULL,   normal.cells = NULL,   bulkdata = NULL,   gdscdata = NULL )

title: Identify Pharmacological Cell Subpopulations — scPharmIdentify
text: object Seurat object containing single-cell RNA-seq data. type Data source type. Either "tissue" tumor tissue samples "cellline" cell line samples. "tissue", function identifies tumor vs adjacent normal cells using CNV analysis. cancer TCGA cancer type(s). character string vector specifying cancer type(s) (e.g., "BRCA", c("LUAD", "LUSC")). Use "pan" pan-cancer analysis. drug Drug name analyze. NULL (default), drugs GDSC2 project analyzed. nmcs Number MCA components compute. Default: 50. nfeatures Number genes cell identity signature. Default: 200. cores Number CPU cores parallel processing. Default: 1. features Character vector gene names use. NULL, features used. slot Slot name Seurat V4 data access. Default: "data". layer Layer name Seurat V5 data access. NULL, uses slot value. assay Assay use. Default: "RNA". threshold.s Threshold labeling sensitive cells. Cells NES value classified sensitive. Default: -1.751302. threshold.r Threshold labeling resistant cells. Cells NES value classified resistant. Default: 1.518551. tumor.cells Character vector known tumor cell barcodes. provided type="tissue", CNV-based detection skipped. normal.cells Character vector known normal cell barcodes. Used reference CNV analysis provided. bulkdata Bulk RNA-seq data cell lines. NULL, uses built-scPharm::bulkdata. gdscdata GDSC pharmacogenomics data. NULL, uses built-scPharm::gdscdata.

title: Identify Pharmacological Cell Subpopulations — scPharmIdentify
text: Seurat object pharmacological annotations added metadata: cell.label Cell type: "tumor" "adjacent" scPharm_label_DRUGID_DRUGNAME Drug response: "sensitive", "resistant", "" scPharm_nes_DRUGID_DRUGNAME Normalized enrichment score drug

title: Identify Pharmacological Cell Subpopulations — scPharmIdentify
text: function performs following steps: tissue samples: identifies tumor cells via CNV analysis (uses provided annotations) Computes Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA) dimensionality reduction Generates cell identity gene signatures Correlates gene expression drug response (AUC) across cell lines Performs GSEA score cell's drug response profile Classifies cells based NES thresholds

title: Identify Pharmacological Cell Subpopulations — scPharmIdentify
text: Tian P, Zheng J, et al. scPharm: identifying pharmacological subpopulations single cells precision medicine cancers. 2023.
